title.narrative: Faith in Action: Strengthening Gender Justice and Inclusive Governance through Community-led Movements

description.narrative:
This 12-month initiative builds on the progress made under the recently concluded project, “Strengthening the Pursuit of Gender Justice by Promoting GBV Prevention and Women’s Leadership in Nairobi, Kitui, and Samburu.” The April 2025 needs assessment showed increased community engagement and awareness around gender justice. However, gaps remain particularly low male involvement, marginalisation of youth and persons with disabilities (PWDs) and limited women’s representation in leadership. To build on the gains, this next phase focuses on three strategic pillars:
Expanding the Side-by-Side Faith Movement for Gender Justice by deepening inclusive, values-based leadership and support participation in the 2025 Africa Regional Gender Justice Conference convened by IFAGE (17th to 19th September 2025) Developing and distributing a contextual Gender Justice Handbook to support faith leaders in advancing gender transformative messages and teaching. Strengthening public engagement through media and grassroots mobilisation, county forums, civic campaigns and storytelling, especially during key moments such as the 16 Days of Activism and International Women’s Day.
A central feature of this phase is the expansion of media engagement. Radio programming from the previous phase will be scaled to include television and social media broadcasts through Family Media, East and Central Africa’s largest Christian media platform. With a multi-platform reach across radio, TV, and digital channels, Family Media provides access to a wide, diverse audience. The media platform played a critical role in elevating public dialogue on gender justice in the previous phase. In this phase, we will integrate short video clips from the three counties, showcasing voices of women leaders, youth, faith actors and survivors of GBV. By connecting local realities with national media, the project will drive empathy, seek to inspire action and strengthen the bridge between communities and the public discourse. Additionally, the project will produce a short documentary as part of its Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) framework. The film will capture community driven change, track project milestones and serve as a learning and advocacy tool. It will be shared with partners and stakeholders during project closure sessions to support reflection, documentation and evidence based influence. The use of video aims to create lasting impact through emotional connection and storytelling.
